title: Payment, Late Charges and Credit Control on Event Invoices
content:
An event bill under Private Event & Banquet Services falls due the number of days after the final bill date printed against the package, and a payment is recorded against the single bill it settles.

## 1. When a payment is accepted

A payment is accepted while the agreement stands active, on hold or closed, since settling arrears is exactly how a hold comes off and a closed agreement may still carry a balance. The state and the unsettled balance are read from the company's records against the agreement's own reference before the payment is taken.

| The records show the agreement | Payment accepted |
| --- | --- |
| Active | Yes |
| On hold | Yes |
| Closed | Yes |
| Proposed | No |

## 2. Part payments and overpayments

A part payment settles the named bill in part and never spills onto another bill; an overpayment leaves the excess on the agreement to be applied to the next bill raised.

## 3. The late charge

A late charge is the monthly late percentage printed against the package applied to the amount still outstanding once the grace days printed against the same package have passed, held to the late charge ceiling printed against that package.

## 4. The window for disputing a final bill

The following clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis: "The client may dispute a final bill no later than the dispute window for the package, counted in calendar days from the day the final bill was raised."

The day-counting convention written under that clause — "Dispute window days are counted as calendar days from the day after the bill was raised, every day of the week counts, and a dispute reaching Larkspur Table on the boundary day itself is in time; calendar days are never converted into full 24-hour periods." — counted from the very anchor that clause set, and it goes with the clause it counted: the day the dispute window runs from is the day the current basis fixes, and the anchor quoted here governs nothing. The dispute window printed against the package is unaffected and remains the figure of the package.

## 5. Credit hold

Once a bill is past due by the credit hold threshold printed against the package, booking stops on the agreement until the balance is settled.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

On a package whose payment terms are 30 days, whose grace is 7 days and whose monthly late percentage is 1.25, a bill of 4000 left wholly unpaid past the grace carries a late charge worked at that monthly percentage on the 4000 still outstanding, and that charge never exceeds the ceiling printed against the package.

superseded_clauses: The client may dispute a final bill no later than the dispute window for the package, counted in calendar days from the day the final bill was raised.
